thread:
evan: Seeing a weird eviction pattern in ap-southeast1 tonight — tiny pods (0.5GPU) are getting OOM/evicted while 2+GPU gangs stay pinned.
jia: same, started ~01:10 UTC. Pod pending -> scheduled -> evicted in ~30s repeatedly :confused:
matt: could be taint/affinity interplay or the new egress QoS patch. Any node-level taints showing?
sofia: @matt ran `kubectl describe node gpu-rack-3b` — shows taint `rack-isolated:NoSchedule` and `egress=limited:NoExecute` on a few nodes.
ev an: infra-bot reported rebalancer backoff earlier: "rebalancer: soft-stop due to network egress spike" at 01:05UTC.
infra-bot: rebalancer: suppressed resyncs for 3m due to az-egress-rate-limit, backlog=420 pods
matt: ok that explains delayed warm-pool healing. tiny pods are being squeezed into leftover slots -> fragmentation. Can we drain a node in the rack and reprovision larger contiguous slots?
jia: we tried compacting but node autoscaler refused to replace because of egress quota. Created a ticket to infra: cloud-provider egress quota at 98% in ap-southeast1c.
sofia: temporary mitigation: added a soft-affinity rule preferring same-rack coalesce for 0.5GPU pods to reduce cross-node shearing, patch applied as rollbackable flag.
evan: rolling that now. If we don't see improvement in 10m we'll scale a spare warm-pool in another AZ to reduce pressure.
matt: followup: need to add a scheduler metric for "tiny-pod fragmentation ratio" and alert before eviction spike. Filed infra task #INF-3287.
sofia: note — this looks costy: overprovision + multiple tiny restarts = extra GPU-hours. estimate ~4 GPU-hours extra in last 2h.
jia: logs snippet:
```
I0312 01:12:05  kubelet eviction_manager.go:237] eviction signal: memory.available
Pod xyz received SIGKILL by eviction
```
evan: thanks team. will watch, ping if you see re-evictions. :thumbsup:
